items.headline: Inflation Data Will Be the Real Test for This AI Stock Rally
items.summary: Barron's frames this week's CPI as the key test for an equity market already absorbing weaker employment. A benign inflation print would support duration and technology; hotter inflation combined with softer labor data would raise stagflation risk and complicate Fed expectations.
items.whyItMatters: Directly affects the valuation regime for growth equities, Treasury yields and the near-term durability of the AI-led rally.

items.headline: Berkshire's Stock Buybacks Among Highest in a Decade
items.summary: Berkshire accelerated repurchases and was a net buyer of equities while retaining an unusually large cash balance. The combination suggests greater willingness to deploy capital under Greg Abel while preserving substantial optionality.
items.whyItMatters: Useful read-through for capital-allocation discipline, market valuation and Berkshire's confidence in its own shares and selected equities.

items.headline: Apple May Turn to China to Solve the Memory Crunch
items.summary: Apple is evaluating Chinese DRAM supply for devices sold in China as memory pricing tightens. The strategic issue is less near-term Apple supply than the potential emergence of a stronger Chinese memory competitor and its longer-term implications for Micron and HBM economics.
items.whyItMatters: Connects supply-chain resilience, U.S.-China policy and semiconductor pricing; potentially material for memory margins and competitive intensity.

items.headline: Why Coca-Cola Is Clobbering PepsiCo
items.summary: Barron's highlights Coca-Cola's asset-light model, stronger category share and Zero-sugar momentum versus PepsiCo's more vertically integrated food-and-beverage structure. The valuation premium reflects higher perceived quality and capital efficiency.
items.whyItMatters: Provides a useful quality-versus-valuation comparison for defensive equity allocation.

items.headline: Mortgage Rates Are All Over the Place. That Could Benefit Buyers.
items.summary: High and volatile mortgage rates continue to suppress transaction volumes, but weaker demand may improve negotiating power for well-capitalized buyers. The opportunity is selective rather than cyclical: affordability remains constrained and financing discipline is essential.
items.whyItMatters: Relevant to AGCI's real-estate framework because financing stress can create acquisition opportunities without implying a broad housing recovery.
